## Changes since `v0.6.1-beta.10`

### Features

- choose a connection's keyword highlight set in the connection dialog: profiles could keep a set but nothing let the user pick one; SSH and serial connections get a Keyword highlighting field that follows the default set, names a set or turns highlighting off, and a set deleted since shows as the default set, which the terminal falls back to as well ([7567fff8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/7567fff88900b8e8baf1c536a9e488fe926b9d3d))
- add a Highlighting settings page for keyword highlight sets: the rules had no place to be seen or changed; the page turns highlighting on or off, picks the default set and whether full-screen programs are highlighted, and edits the sets: add, copy, rename and delete sets, restore the built-in rules, and add, order, toggle and edit rules with their match type, case, whole word and colors from the theme's palette or a custom one; a pattern is saved once valid, with the error shown while typing, and a preview colors sample output, or the user's own, as the set would; each edit builds on the one before it is saved, since settings are saved whole ([1170476f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/1170476f9457a92e19766cbc4a6c4560c1d12523))
- highlight keywords in terminal output as it appears: with the sets in place, terminals color what they match without the user searching for it; each terminal loads a KeywordHighlighter addon that colors matches with xterm decorations, so copied text, logs and searches still see the output as sent, and only the lines on screen and a screen around them carry decorations, matched again only when their text changes, so a flood of output or a long scrollback costs no more; full-screen programs are left alone unless the setting asks, a hidden tab catches up when shown, the colors follow the connection's theme, and the terminal's context menu can pause highlighting for that tab ([400c0f9c](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/400c0f9c615b1756c622f882fcf80427d10a9511))
- keep keyword highlight sets in the config and let connections pick one: the sets need to be saved, synced and backed up like other settings, and a connection to a switch wants other rules than one to a web server; the config gains keyword_highlight (on or off, the default set, whether full-screen programs are highlighted, and the sets, unset while the built-in set applies so its rules improve with tTerm), synced across devices, and SSH and serial profiles a highlight_set that names a set or off and follows the default set when unset, which an ssh_config import keeps ([0efa0ae0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/0efa0ae0fc8066d06a1492c958bc2946ccdacae0))
- match keywords in terminal text for highlighting: operators and network engineers rely on Xshell's highlight sets and SecureCRT's keyword highlighting to spot error, denied or an IP address in a flood of output, and tTerm had nothing like it; src/lib/keywordHighlight holds named sets of keyword or regex rules with optional case and whole-word matching and a text and background color each, a palette color name that follows the terminal theme or a hex color, a built-in set (errors, warnings, successes, IPv4, IPv6 that needs a digit so Add::add stays plain, MAC addresses), the matching that lets the earlier rule win where matches overlap and caps the text and highlights per line, and the reading of buffer rows into text with the cell behind each character, wrapped rows and wide characters included, skipping cells the program colored itself ([580758f3](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/580758f35cf78617c135dd0896a7f27a17d52f9a))
- take the terminal to a folder from the SFTP drawer: going the other way, from a folder found in the file panel to a shell in it, meant copying the path and typing cd; the drawer's header gets a button for the listed folder and a folder's context menu an "Open in Terminal" item, which type cd with the path escaped at this tab's prompt (not at the tabs it broadcasts to) and show the terminal, and say the terminal is busy instead while an editor, a pager or a command shell integration saw start has it ([462edfa5](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/462edfa5a4d14c0f80afab1288480e41284c7ad6))
- let the SFTP drawer open at home, the last directory or the terminal's directory, and follow the terminal: users cd in the terminal and expect the file panel to go along, as FinalShell, MobaXterm and Xshell do, but the drawer ignored what remote shells report and always resumed the last directory; a new SFTP setting picks where drawers open (the last directory stays the default, so nothing changes until it is set), a connection can choose otherwise, and a toggle in the drawer follows each directory the shell reports with OSC 7, on from the start for drawers that open at the terminal's directory; remote reports go to a store of their own so they never reach the local tab's restart directory, a directory SFTP cannot list falls back to where the drawer opens otherwise and is not retried, a hidden drawer catches up when shown, and the toggle says when the shell reports nothing because the connection lacks Shell integration ([a9a8f689](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/a9a8f6890c40486d33972d21a6c088db50e47530))
- report the remote shell's directory even with command marks off: the SFTP drawer is going to follow the terminal's directory, which the remote scripts already report (OSC 7) at every prompt, but turning Mark commands off in Settings skipped installing them altogether; the install now goes ahead and starts the shell with tterm_marks=0, so it only reports the directory, and the "marks off" reason goes away; the scripts to paste into ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc or config.fish report the directory too ([224cf07a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/224cf07aa49ba33f3196d96cd228483223d441c2))

### Fixes

- keep bash's prompt hook when a profile assigns PROMPT_COMMAND: bash got the hook through the environment before it read the login files, so a ~/.bash_profile or ~/.bashrc with PROMPT_COMMAND="history -a" dropped it, and with it the directory reports the SFTP drawer follows and the command marks; start.sh now runs bash --posix --login, which reads only $ENV, and bash/init.bash leaves POSIX mode, reads the login files in bash's order and then puts the hook first in PROMPT_COMMAND, keeping a login shell and ~/.bash_history; the hook and PROMPT_COMMAND are no longer exported, so a shell started with su does not report its directory; macOS's own bash reads the login files even in POSIX mode and never $ENV, so it keeps the hook up front; the real-shell tests now replace PROMPT_COMMAND in the profile, check the directory report, and cover command marks off ([721e85da](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/721e85da01ceec55db835d05faac3d9ded862d6f))
- connect to servers whose only host key is RSA: russh was built without its rsa feature to keep RUSTSEC-2023-0071 out, so it could not verify RSA host keys and tTerm stopped offering them, which locked out CentOS 6 and much network equipment; that advisory is a timing leak in private-key operations, while checking a host key uses only the server's public key, and tTerm keeps signing with RSA key files through ring, so the feature is now on; RSA stays after Ed25519 and ECDSA so a server with both keeps presenting the key it was trusted with, and SHA-1 ssh-rsa comes last; the explanation for an unverifiable host now names the DSA-only servers it still applies to ([84dbec0b](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/84dbec0b323893df5a411ed88e3fb0b12db1d2f0))

### Other changes

- drop the comparison table from the READMEs: ranking tTerm against other clients reads as talking them down, and the reasons to choose tTerm already stand on their own ([3d26e7db](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3d26e7dbe5ccb2dacb8b06da7b40721c9f66caae))
- rewrite the READMEs to sell tTerm and move developer docs to CONTRIBUTING.md: visitors decide in seconds, but the first screen was a long feature list with the download link 200 lines down, so it now opens with the pitch, badges and download, then the reasons to switch, a comparison with Xshell, SecureCRT, Termius and Tabby checked against their public docs, install steps per platform, the macOS fixes for the first-launch "damaged" block (quarantine removal) and the Keychain prompt after every update (no Developer ID), collapsible feature lists and a FAQ; build, scripts, architecture and release notes move to CONTRIBUTING.md, whose checks now match AGENTS.md and CI ([2981043e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2981043e433ea835ba4064080907c27ce6a67b56))
